## About

Daniel Palacios is a Ph.D. candidate in Quantitative and Computational
Biosciences at Baylor College of Medicine (2022–2027) and an NSF Graduate
Research Fellow. He works in the Liu Lab at Texas Children's Hospital's Duncan
Neurological Research Institute, where he applies AI and machine learning —
LLM-powered agentic systems, multi-agent architectures, and EHR foundation
models — to clinical informatics and computational biology. His projects span
postpartum mental-health prediction, pediatric diabetes outcomes,
treatment-response phenotyping, clinical-note de-identification, and pediatric
disease-trajectory modeling. He was previously a Research Associate at NASA
Ames Research Center (space radiation biology) and a Machine Learning
Researcher Intern at NASA Johnson Space Center (NLP for engineering failure
reports), and did undergraduate research in theoretical superconductivity at
the University of Houston, where he earned a B.S. in Physics and Mathematics in
2022. His work has appeared in Physical Review B, Scientific Reports, and
Pregnancy, with manuscripts under review at JAMIA and PLOS Digital Health and
a preprint on arXiv.
